question.text: What kind of copies of checklist documents does the Driver Service Center accept?

answer.text: Every document on the application checklist must be an original or a certified copy; faxes and photocopies are turned away.

teaching.text: A fax or photocopy will be turned away, so bring the original or a certified copy of every checklist item. Remember: Originals only, no photocopies.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: Every document on the application checklist must be an original or a certified copy; faxes and photocopies are turned away.

question.text: Why does the Department ask every applicant to prove full legal name and date of birth?

answer.text: The Department asks every applicant to prove full legal name and date of birth so it can confirm identity and reduce fraud.

teaching.text: Proving full legal name and date of birth lets the Department confirm identity and reduce fraud. Remember: Prove who, prevent fraud.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: The Department asks every applicant to prove full legal name and date of birth so it can confirm identity and reduce fraud.

question.text: What can document verification do to issuance?

answer.text: Every document is subject to verification with the agency that issued it, and that verification can delay issuance of a permit, license or ID.

teaching.text: Because documents are checked with their issuers, verification can slow down issuance. Remember: Checking can cause delays.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: Every document is subject to verification with the agency that issued it, and that verification can delay issuance of a permit, license or ID.

question.text: How do Primary and Secondary identification items differ?

answer.text: Primary identification includes items such as a certified birth certificate, a valid passport, a military ID or a photo license from another state, while Secondary identification covers supporting items such as check stubs, union cards, work IDs and tax forms.

teaching.text: Primary items are core documents like passports; Secondary items like work IDs support them. Remember: Primary core, Secondary support.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: Primary identification includes items such as a certified birth certificate, a valid passport, a military ID or a photo license from another state, while Secondary identification covers supporting items such as check stubs, union cards, work IDs and tax forms.

question.text: When does a computerized check stub count as identification?

answer.text: A computerized check stub counts as secondary identification only when the applicant's full name is pre-printed on it.

teaching.text: A computerized check stub only counts when your full name is pre-printed on it. Remember: Name must be pre-printed.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: A computerized check stub counts as secondary identification only when the applicant's full name is pre-printed on it.

question.text: What kind of Social Security card is accepted as identification?

answer.text: A Social Security card used as identification must be the original, never a metal or plastic replica.

teaching.text: Metal and plastic replica cards are refused; only the original Social Security card works. Remember: Original card, no replicas.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: A Social Security card used as identification must be the original, never a metal or plastic replica.

question.text: How many identity items does an original applicant need, and from which lists?

answer.text: The examiner asks for two identity items, and an original applicant must supply at least one from the Primary list, with the second from either list.

teaching.text: A first license needs at least one Primary item; the second can come from either list. Remember: One must be Primary.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: The examiner asks for two identity items, and an original applicant must supply at least one from the Primary list, with the second from either list.

question.text: What identity items do duplicate or renewal applicants need?

answer.text: Applicants for a duplicate or renewal of an existing Tennessee license or ID may supply any two identity items from either list.

teaching.text: Renewals and duplicates are more flexible: any two items from either list will do. Remember: Renewals pick any two.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: Applicants for a duplicate or renewal of an existing Tennessee license or ID may supply any two identity items from either list.

question.text: What must new residents do with the license from their former state?

answer.text: New residents must hand in the license from their former state, and if it was lost they provide the same two identity items as an original applicant.

teaching.text: New residents give up the old license, and a lost one is replaced by the original applicant's two identity items. Remember: Hand in the old card.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: New residents must hand in the license from their former state, and if it was lost they provide the same two identity items as an original applicant.

question.text: What kind of birth certificate is accepted, and which kinds are refused?

answer.text: A birth certificate must be certified, sealed and issued by an authorized agency such as the Bureau of Vital Statistics, and hospital-issued or baptismal certificates are refused.

teaching.text: Only a certified, sealed certificate from an authorized agency counts; hospital and baptismal certificates do not. Remember: Sealed and certified only.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: A birth certificate must be certified, sealed and issued by an authorized agency such as the Bureau of Vital Statistics, and hospital-issued or baptismal certificates are refused.

question.text: What rules apply to passports and documents not in English?

answer.text: An expired passport is not accepted, and a passport, birth certificate or license not written in English must come with a Certificate of Accurate Translation.

teaching.text: Passports must be current, and documents not in English need a Certificate of Accurate Translation. Remember: No expired passports, translate.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: An expired passport is not accepted, and a passport, birth certificate or license not written in English must come with a Certificate of Accurate Translation.

question.text: What can a new resident's former state license prove, and what can it never prove?

answer.text: A new resident's valid license from the former state can prove identity, but it never proves US citizenship or lawful permanent residency.

teaching.text: An out-of-state license helps prove identity, but status still needs its own document. Remember: Proves identity, not citizenship.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: A new resident's valid license from the former state can prove identity, but it never proves US citizenship or lawful permanent residency.

question.text: Which applicants must prove US citizenship or lawful permanent residency?

answer.text: Proof of US citizenship or lawful permanent residency is required of first-time applicants, new and returning residents, anyone reinstating after a revocation, suspension or cancellation, and anyone licensed since January one, two thousand one who is renewing for the first time.

teaching.text: Status proof is required at the start, on return, at reinstatement and at certain first renewals. Remember: First-timers, newcomers, reinstaters.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: Proof of US citizenship or lawful permanent residency is required of first-time applicants, new and returning residents, anyone reinstating after a revocation, suspension or cancellation, and anyone licensed since January one, two thousand one who is renewing for the first time.

question.text: Which documents prove US citizenship or permanent residency?

answer.text: Accepted proof of citizenship or permanent residency includes a certified birth certificate from a US state or territory, a valid US passport, a Certificate of Citizenship or Naturalization, and an I-five hundred fifty-one Permanent Resident card.

teaching.text: A certified birth certificate, a valid passport or a citizenship, naturalization or residency document proves status. Remember: Birth certificate, passport, certificates.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: Accepted proof of citizenship or permanent residency includes a certified birth certificate from a US state or territory, a valid US passport, a Certificate of Citizenship or Naturalization, and an I-five hundred fifty-one Permanent Resident card.

question.text: What must people first licensed after the start of two thousand one do at their first renewal?

answer.text: Anyone first issued a Tennessee license or photo ID after January one, two thousand one must show citizenship or permanent-residency documents at the first renewal and cannot renew that time by mail or online.

teaching.text: The first renewal after a post two thousand one license must be done in person with status documents. Remember: First renewal in person.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: Anyone first issued a Tennessee license or photo ID after January one, two thousand one must show citizenship or permanent-residency documents at the first renewal and cannot renew that time by mail or online.

question.text: What can an applicant with only temporary legal presence get?

answer.text: An applicant who has only temporary legal presence cannot get a regular license or ID, but may qualify for a Temporary Driver License or Temporary Identification License by proving authorized stay.

teaching.text: Temporary legal presence leads to a TDL or TID, never a regular license or ID. Remember: Temporary license, not regular.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: An applicant who has only temporary legal presence cannot get a regular license or ID, but may qualify for a Temporary Driver License or Temporary Identification License by proving authorized stay.

question.text: Do TDL and TID applicants still meet Tennessee examination requirements?

answer.text: A TDL or TID applicant must still meet every Tennessee examination requirement for driving Class XD or Class XM vehicles.

teaching.text: A temporary credential does not lower the bar: every examination requirement still applies. Remember: Same exams for X classes.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: A TDL or TID applicant must still meet every Tennessee examination requirement for driving Class XD or Class XM vehicles.

question.text: How long does a TDL or TID last, and how are its base and extra fees set?

answer.text: A Temporary Driver License or Temporary Identification License runs for the authorized stay up to five years at a fixed twenty-eight-dollar base rate regardless of duration, plus any applicable GDL, motorcycle, or multi-type fees.

teaching.text: Every temporary credential costs the same flat fee and lasts for the authorized stay, up to five years. Remember: Twenty-eight base, plus extra fees.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: A Temporary Driver License or Temporary Identification License runs for the authorized stay up to five years at a fixed twenty-eight-dollar base rate regardless of duration, plus any applicable GDL, motorcycle, or multi-type fees.

question.text: What residency proof must every applicant bring, and how current must it be?

answer.text: Applicants bring two proofs of Tennessee residency showing their name and street address, with no post office boxes, and each must be current, meaning dated within the last four months.

teaching.text: Both residency proofs need your street address and a date within the last four months; post office boxes do not count. Remember: Two proofs, four months fresh.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: Applicants bring two proofs of Tennessee residency showing their name and street address, with no post office boxes, and each must be current, meaning dated within the last four months.

question.text: Which documents count as proof of Tennessee residency?

answer.text: Acceptable residency proofs include a current utility bill with its postmarked envelope, a bank statement, a signed lease or mortgage, an insurance policy, Tennessee vehicle or voter registration, a W-two, or a property tax receipt from within the last year.

teaching.text: Statements, leases, policies, registrations and tax papers count as residency proof. Remember: Bills, leases, statements count.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: Acceptable residency proofs include a current utility bill with its postmarked envelope, a bank statement, a signed lease or mortgage, an insurance policy, Tennessee vehicle or voter registration, a W-two, or a property tax receipt from within the last year.

question.text: Which documents do not count as proof of residency?

answer.text: A utility initial deposit receipt, bank checks and insurance wallet cards do not count as proof of residency.

teaching.text: Deposit receipts, bank checks and insurance wallet cards may seem convincing but do not prove residency. Remember: Deposit slips and wallet cards fail.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: A utility initial deposit receipt, bank checks and insurance wallet cards do not count as proof of residency.
audio_scripts.must_match_memory_hook: Deposit slips and wallet cards fail

question.text: Which applicants must show residency proof?

answer.text: Residency proof is demanded from first-time, new-resident and returning-resident applicants for every ID, TDL, permit and license class, even if they once held a Tennessee license before moving away.

teaching.text: Holding a Tennessee license in the past does not excuse a returning resident from residency proof. Remember: Every first, new or returning applicant.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: Residency proof is demanded from first-time, new-resident and returning-resident applicants for every ID, TDL, permit and license class, even if they once held a Tennessee license before moving away.
audio_scripts.must_match_memory_hook: Every first, new or returning applicant

question.text: Whose name may appear on residency documents?

answer.text: Residency documents may name the applicant, the applicant's spouse, or for a minor a parent or legal guardian, and relationship is then shown with a certified marriage certificate or long-form birth certificate.

teaching.text: A spouse's name, or a parent's or guardian's for a minor, can appear on the proof if the relationship is documented. Remember: Spouse or parent may count.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: Residency documents may name the applicant, the applicant's spouse, or for a minor a parent or legal guardian, and relationship is then shown with a certified marriage certificate or long-form birth certificate.

question.text: When must your Social Security number appear on the application, and is it printed on the license?

answer.text: Tennessee law requires your Social Security number on the application whenever the US Government has issued you one, and the number is kept on your record but never printed on the license.

teaching.text: The number is required when one was issued, but it stays on your record and off the card. Remember: On record, never printed.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: Tennessee law requires your Social Security number on the application whenever the US Government has issued you one, and the number is kept on your record but never printed on the license.

question.text: What happens if your Social Security number does not match federal records?

answer.text: If the Social Security number does not match federal records, the examiner asks for more proof and may send you to the Social Security Administration before accepting the application.

teaching.text: A mismatch with federal records means the examiner asks for more proof before accepting the application. Remember: Mismatch means more proof.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: If the Social Security number does not match federal records, the examiner asks for more proof and may send you to the Social Security Administration before accepting the application.

question.text: What must someone never issued a Social Security number do?

answer.text: Someone never issued a Social Security number must sign a sworn affidavit in person before an examiner or notary, under penalty of perjury, and must sign a new one with every later application.

teaching.text: The sworn affidavit replaces the number, and it must be signed again in person with every application. Remember: Sworn affidavit every time.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: Someone never issued a Social Security number must sign a sworn affidavit in person before an examiner or notary, under penalty of perjury, and must sign a new one with every later application.

question.text: Which documents can prove a Social Security number?

answer.text: A Social Security number can be proven with an original card, a W-two showing the full number, an employer payroll stub or bank statement with the number, or a health insurance card showing name and number.

teaching.text: A card, a W-two, a payroll stub, a bank statement or a health insurance card showing the number can prove it. Remember: Card, W-two, stub, statement.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: A Social Security number can be proven with an original card, a W-two showing the full number, an employer payroll stub or bank statement with the number, or a health insurance card showing name and number.

question.text: What extra papers does an applicant under eighteen need for financial responsibility?

answer.text: An applicant under eighteen also needs a Teenage Affidavit for financial responsibility, plus proof of relationship such as custody, adoption or marriage papers when the signing guardian or step-parent is not named on school attendance records.

teaching.text: The Teenage Affidavit covers financial responsibility, and relationship papers are added when the signer is not on school records. Remember: Teen affidavit, family proof.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: An applicant under eighteen also needs a Teenage Affidavit for financial responsibility, plus proof of relationship such as custody, adoption or marriage papers when the signing guardian or step-parent is not named on school attendance records.

question.text: What school proof does an applicant under eighteen need?

answer.text: An applicant under eighteen needs proof of school attendance or progress, such as Form SF1010 completed by the principal or guidance teacher, signed and dated within the past thirty days.

teaching.text: The school form must be recent: signed and dated within the past thirty days. Remember: School form, signed recently.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: An applicant under eighteen needs proof of school attendance or progress, such as Form SF1010 completed by the principal or guidance teacher, signed and dated within the past thirty days.

question.text: What form must a teen moving past the learner permit submit, and when?

answer.text: A teen moving past the learner permit must submit form SF-one thousand two hundred fifty-six certifying fifty hours of behind-the-wheel experience, after holding the permit for six months.

teaching.text: The fifty-hour certification comes after six months on the permit, separate from the school form. Remember: Fifty hours, six months.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: A teen moving past the learner permit must submit form SF-one thousand two hundred fifty-six certifying fifty hours of behind-the-wheel experience, after holding the permit for six months.

question.text: Who does the Graduated Driver License program not apply to?

answer.text: The Graduated Driver License program does not apply to anyone eighteen or older, or to anyone under eighteen who has graduated high school or earned a GED.

teaching.text: Turning eighteen, graduating high school or earning a GED takes an applicant outside the GDL program. Remember: Eighteen or graduated skips.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: The Graduated Driver License program does not apply to anyone eighteen or older, or to anyone under eighteen who has graduated high school or earned a GED.

question.text: What documents support a name change, and can it be done by mail?

answer.text: Every supporting document for a name change must be an original or certified legal paper, and name changes are never accepted by mail.

teaching.text: Name changes always need original or certified legal papers, and they cannot be mailed in. Remember: Certified papers, in person.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: Every supporting document for a name change must be an original or certified legal paper, and name changes are never accepted by mail.

question.text: Which marriage document supports a name change?

answer.text: For a marriage name change, the certificate must be the original or certified copy registered after the wedding, not the license that authorized it.

teaching.text: The marriage certificate registered after the wedding is what counts, not the license issued before it. Remember: Certificate, not license.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: For a marriage name change, the certificate must be the original or certified copy registered after the wedding, not the license that authorized it.

question.text: When is a copy of a court document acceptable?

answer.text: A court-document copy is acceptable only if the original signature or seal is affixed to it, and a copy with a copied seal or signature is refused.

teaching.text: A court copy needs its original signature or seal attached; copied seals are refused. Remember: Original seal on the copy.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: A court-document copy is acceptable only if the original signature or seal is affixed to it, and a copy with a copied seal or signature is refused.

question.text: How soon must a new resident with another state's license get a Tennessee license?

answer.text: New or returning residents holding another state's license must get a Tennessee license within thirty days of establishing residency.

teaching.text: The thirty-day clock starts when you establish residency, not when your old license expires. Remember: Thirty days to switch.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: New or returning residents holding another state's license must get a Tennessee license within thirty days of establishing residency.

question.text: Which test does every new or returning resident take?

answer.text: Every new or returning resident takes a Tennessee vision screening at the Driver Service Center.

teaching.text: Every new or returning resident takes the vision screening, even when no other test is needed. Remember: Vision for every newcomer.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: Every new or returning resident takes a Tennessee vision screening at the Driver Service Center.

question.text: When must a new resident pass the knowledge, road and vision tests?

answer.text: A new or returning resident whose out-of-state license expired more than six months ago must pass the knowledge exam, the road skills test and the vision screening.

teaching.text: Full testing is triggered by a license expired more than six months, not by moving itself. Remember: Expired over six months, retest.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: A new or returning resident whose out-of-state license expired more than six months ago must pass the knowledge exam, the road skills test and the vision screening.

question.text: How do the thirty-day and six-month new-resident limits differ?

answer.text: Two look-alike new-resident limits: a newcomer has thirty days after establishing residency to switch to a Tennessee license, but only an out-of-state license expired more than six months triggers the full knowledge, road and vision testing.

teaching.text: Thirty days is the switching deadline; six months is the expiry point that brings full testing. Remember: Switch by thirty, retest past six.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: Two look-alike new-resident limits: a newcomer has thirty days after establishing residency to switch to a Tennessee license, but only an out-of-state license expired more than six months triggers the full knowledge, road and vision testing.
audio_scripts.must_match_memory_hook: Switch by thirty, retest past six

question.text: What tests do new residents from other countries take, and may they keep their foreign license?

answer.text: New residents arriving from other countries take the vision screening, knowledge exam and road skills test, and they may keep their foreign license.

teaching.text: Drivers from other countries take all three tests but may keep their foreign license. Remember: All three tests, keep it.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: New residents arriving from other countries take the vision screening, knowledge exam and road skills test, and they may keep their foreign license.

question.text: When does a service member's Tennessee license stay valid past its expiration?

answer.text: A Tennessee license held by a member of the US Armed Forces stays valid past its printed expiration while the person is on active duty based outside Tennessee and the license is not surrendered, canceled or suspended.

teaching.text: The extension depends on active duty outside Tennessee and a license that was not surrendered, canceled or suspended. Remember: Active duty elsewhere extends.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: A Tennessee license held by a member of the US Armed Forces stays valid past its printed expiration while the person is on active duty based outside Tennessee and the license is not surrendered, canceled or suspended.

question.text: How can active-duty personnel outside Tennessee show their license does not expire?

answer.text: Active-duty personnel stationed outside Tennessee may have Code thirty added to the license to show it does not expire, by bringing their military orders and paying the fee.

teaching.text: Code thirty on the license shows it does not expire, and adding it takes military orders and the fee. Remember: Code thirty with orders.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: Active-duty personnel stationed outside Tennessee may have Code thirty added to the license to show it does not expire, by bringing their military orders and paying the fee.

question.text: How soon must a service member renew after returning to Tennessee?

answer.text: After discharge, separation or reassignment back to Tennessee, the service member must renew within sixty days, and Fort Campbell counts as a Tennessee assignment.

teaching.text: The sixty-day renewal clock starts on returning to Tennessee, and Fort Campbell counts as Tennessee. Remember: Sixty days after return.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: After discharge, separation or reassignment back to Tennessee, the service member must renew within sixty days, and Fort Campbell counts as a Tennessee assignment.

question.text: Who cannot use the active-duty license extension?

answer.text: Members of the National Guard and family members of military personnel cannot use the active-duty license extension.

teaching.text: National Guard members and military families cannot use the active-duty extension. Remember: Guard and families excluded.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: Members of the National Guard and family members of military personnel cannot use the active-duty license extension.

question.text: How long do licenses for people over twenty-one run since the start of two thousand sixteen?

answer.text: Since January one, two thousand sixteen, licenses for people over twenty-one run eight years from the issue date, so they usually no longer expire on a birthday.

teaching.text: Newer adult licenses run eight years from the issue date rather than ending on a birthday. Remember: Eight years, not birthdays.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: Since January one, two thousand sixteen, licenses for people over twenty-one run eight years from the issue date, so they usually no longer expire on a birthday.

question.text: When does a Class D license issued before two thousand sixteen expire, and when does a permit expire?

answer.text: A Class D license issued before January one, two thousand sixteen normally expires after five years on your birthdate, while permits normally expire one year after issuance.

teaching.text: Older Class D licenses ended on a birthday after five years, while permits end one year after issuance. Remember: Five years, birthdate.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: A Class D license issued before January one, two thousand sixteen normally expires after five years on your birthdate, while permits normally expire one year after issuance.

question.text: What do a Class D license and an under-eighteen learner permit cost on the standard fee table?

answer.text: On the standard eight-year fee table, a Class D operator license costs twenty-eight dollars with a minimum age of sixteen, and a learner permit for someone under eighteen costs ten dollars and fifty cents for one year with a minimum age of fifteen.

teaching.text: On the standard table, Class D costs twenty-eight dollars and the under-eighteen permit costs ten dollars and fifty cents. Remember: Class D costs more.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: On the standard eight-year fee table, a Class D operator license costs twenty-eight dollars with a minimum age of sixteen, and a learner permit for someone under eighteen costs ten dollars and fifty cents for one year with a minimum age of fifteen.

question.text: How does the learner permit fee differ by age?

answer.text: A learner permit for someone under eighteen costs ten dollars and fifty cents for one year, while a permit for someone over eighteen costs five dollars and fifty cents for one year.

teaching.text: Younger permit applicants pay more: ten dollars and fifty cents under eighteen, five dollars and fifty cents over. Remember: Under eighteen pays more.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: A learner permit for someone under eighteen costs ten dollars and fifty cents for one year, while a permit for someone over eighteen costs five dollars and fifty cents for one year.

question.text: Which payment methods do Driver Service Centers accept?

answer.text: Driver Service Centers accept cash, check, money order, MasterCard, Visa and Discover for a license or ID.

teaching.text: Centers accept cash, checks, money orders and the major listed cards. Remember: Cash, check, cards accepted.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: Driver Service Centers accept cash, check, money order, MasterCard, Visa and Discover for a license or ID.

question.text: Where can you replace a lost license, and what cannot be replaced online?

answer.text: A lost, stolen or destroyed license, permit or ID can be replaced at any Driver Service Center or sometimes online, but TDLs and TIDs cannot be replaced online.

teaching.text: Most cards can be replaced at a center or sometimes online, but temporary credentials must be replaced in person. Remember: No online temporary replacements.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: A lost, stolen or destroyed license, permit or ID can be replaced at any Driver Service Center or sometimes online, but TDLs and TIDs cannot be replaced online.

question.text: When does the Department mail a courtesy renewal notice?

answer.text: The Department mails a courtesy renewal notice eight to ten weeks before your license expires, though you can renew without it.

teaching.text: The courtesy notice is a reminder, not a requirement; you may renew without it. Remember: Notice weeks ahead.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: The Department mails a courtesy renewal notice eight to ten weeks before your license expires, though you can renew without it.

question.text: What happens when you renew a license that expired long ago?

answer.text: A license expired more than thirty days carries a five dollars late fee, which doubles to ten dollars after six months, and after five years you must also pass the vision, knowledge and skills tests.

teaching.text: The late fee grows from five to ten dollars after six months, and after five years the tests come back. Remember: Late fee grows, then retest.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: A license expired more than thirty days carries a five dollars late fee, which doubles to ten dollars after six months, and after five years you must also pass the vision, knowledge and skills tests.

question.text: Is there a grace period for driving after your license expires?

answer.text: There is no grace period: once your license expires you may not drive, and you face the same penalties as someone never licensed.

teaching.text: An expired license means no driving at all, with the same penalties as never having been licensed. Remember: Expired means stop driving.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: There is no grace period: once your license expires you may not drive, and you face the same penalties as someone never licensed.

question.text: Which drivers may choose a non-photo license, and why might a photo still help?

answer.text: Drivers sixty or older may choose a non-photo license by mail or internet, though a photo license helps with boarding flights, Amtrak and cruise ships.

teaching.text: Drivers sixty or older may choose a non-photo license, though a photo license helps for flights, Amtrak and cruises. Remember: Sixty plus, photo still helps.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: Drivers sixty or older may choose a non-photo license by mail or internet, though a photo license helps with boarding flights, Amtrak and cruise ships.

question.text: How soon must you report a residence address change, even without moving?

answer.text: State law requires you to report a residence address change to the Department of Safety within ten days, even when the change comes from the Postal Service or a nine-one-one district renaming rather than a move.

teaching.text: Even a street renaming by the Postal Service counts as an address change to report within ten days. Remember: Ten days, even renamed streets.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: State law requires you to report a residence address change to the Department of Safety within ten days, even when the change comes from the Postal Service or a nine-one-one district renaming rather than a move.

question.text: What address must your license show?

answer.text: Your license must show a legal residential address with house or apartment number, street, city and zip code, and a post office box alone is refused.

teaching.text: Your license needs a full street address; a post office box alone is refused. Remember: Real street address only.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: Your license must show a legal residential address with house or apartment number, street, city and zip code, and a post office box alone is refused.

question.text: After an address change, what must be updated and what need not be reissued?

answer.text: Two look-alike address rules: the Department record must be updated within ten days of an address change, but the printed license itself does not have to be reissued.

teaching.text: The Department record must change within ten days; the printed card can stay as it is. Remember: Record yes, card no.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: Two look-alike address rules: the Department record must be updated within ten days of an address change, but the printed license itself does not have to be reissued.

question.text: What does the federal Driver Privacy Protection Act do?

answer.text: The federal Driver Privacy Protection Act bars release of personal information from your driving record without your express consent.

teaching.text: Federal law keeps personal information on your driving record private unless you expressly consent. Remember: Your consent, your record.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: The federal Driver Privacy Protection Act bars release of personal information from your driving record without your express consent.

hooks_spoken: Bring originals or certified copies, because faxes and photocopies are turned away.
An original applicant needs two identity items, at least one from the Primary list, while renewals may use any two.
recap.narration_text: Time for a quick review of documents and identification. Bring originals or certified copies, because faxes and photocopies are turned away.
